metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Tillmans Corner, AL
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Tillmans Corner, AL, in south Mobile County? We check your parcel against the Gulf Coast oil and gas trend and offer a written cash price.
heroLead: Most of what we handle out of Tillmans Corner is a family holding a small fractional interest that was never split up cleanly when the land was sold for development.
intro: Tillmans Corner grew fast as Mobile's southwestern suburbs filled in, and a lot of the older parcels in the area were farmland or timberland before that growth, land that in many cases had its mineral rights reserved or sold off separately from the surface decades earlier. If your family kept land in this part of Mobile County going back a few generations, there's a real chance a mineral interest survived even after the surface was subdivided into the neighborhoods that make up Tillmans Corner today.

We start every review here the same way: confirm the legal description, trace it against Mobile County's oil and gas records, and tell you plainly whether the parcel is near meaningful Gulf Coast trend activity or sits further off it.

sections.heading: A suburb built over reserved mineral estates
paragraphs: It's common in this part of Mobile County for a developer to have purchased only the surface decades ago, with the seller's family keeping the mineral rights as part of the deal, sometimes without either side fully realizing what that meant at the time. Those reservations show up in the deed chain even when nobody in the family remembers agreeing to keep them.

If you've never received a lease offer or a royalty check but you know your family sold land in the Tillmans Corner area, it's worth a quick title check. We can usually tell within a day or two whether a mineral reservation exists on your family's old parcel.

sections.heading: Distance from the active Gulf Coast trend
paragraphs: The most active oil and gas structures in Mobile County, including the Hatters Pond gas field and the broader Norphlet and Smackover trend, sit generally east and south of Tillmans Corner. Parcels here tend to be priced as speculative rather than currently producing, which affects how we structure an offer: we're not weighing recent royalty checks, we're weighing how the county's trend has moved historically and whether nearby leasing activity suggests renewed interest.

That's still a real market. Buyers hold speculative acreage in the hope that either commodity prices or new seismic data extend interest further into the county, and we price accordingly rather than assuming zero value simply because a tract has never produced.

sections.heading: What we need from a Tillmans Corner family
paragraphs: The fastest path to an offer is your deed or probate file, or even just the names of the family members who originally owned the land and roughly when it sold. From there we run the title, check current well and unit maps, and come back with a number and the reasoning behind it in writing.

If there are multiple heirs involved, which is common with land held for a few generations, we can work with the group directly and keep everyone informed rather than requiring one person to coordinate the whole transaction.

faqs.question: How do I know if my family kept mineral rights when we sold land near Tillmans Corner?
faqs.answer: The original deed will say so explicitly if a reservation exists. If you don't have the deed, we can pull it from Mobile County Probate Court records using the seller's name and approximate sale date.

faqs.question: Is Tillmans Corner in an active drilling area?
faqs.answer: It sits west of the county's most active Gulf Coast structures, so most interest here is speculative rather than currently producing, though we still check your specific parcel against current permits before pricing it.

faqs.question: There are five of us who inherited this interest together. Do you buy from groups of heirs?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's a common situation and we handle it regularly, keeping every co-owner informed and documented through the process.
